subject: Post-demo: mapping token volumes to unit economics + batching assumptions

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: mapping token volumes to unit economics + batching assumptions

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the few items we promised to follow up on so you have everything in one place.

1) Workload profile you described
- Core flow: user-initiated summarization + short suggestions; median request ~120 tokens in, ~220 tokens out.
- Usage shape: steady baseline (concurrent users across timezone) with predictable daytime peaks; expect bursts tied to batch analytics jobs we discussed.
- Planned ramp: 1M tokens/day month 1, 3–4M tokens/day by month 3, target steady state ~10M tokens/day within 6–9 months if PoC succeeds.

2) Pricing targets and unit economics
- You mentioned target spend guidance of roughly $300–450 per 1M tokens as your internal target for vendor unit cost.
- You also noted total monthly budget range (POC): $3k–$12k depending on trajectory.

3) Batching & concurrency assumptions we discussed
- You prefer continuous batching (server-side prefix caching + small batching windows) to keep latency predictable for interactive flows.
- Expected concurrency: typical interactive concurrency ~4–8 simultaneous inference streams, with short spikes up to ~40 concurrent streams during batch runs.
- Target tail latency: 200–350 ms 95p for interactive requests.

4) Deliverables we’ll provide by EOD Monday:
- A conservative token-econ estimate workbook (attached) with 3 scenarios (low/med/high).
- A short write-up of continuous-batching tuning we recommend for the first 60 days (attached).

Next steps:
- You to confirm the 1M/day initial assumption or provide a corrected monthly/day level sample.
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute pricing deep-dive with Rishi to align on committed capacity vs hosted usage.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Best,

Thanks Priya — this is exactly what I needed. Couple clarifications:

- The 1M/day is conservative for the PoC; more realistic start is 1.5M/day with a steady 4–5% daily growth during the pilot.
- The $300–450/1M target is per our procurement band; for long-term we’re aiming to get below $275/1M with committed capacity.
- For concurrency: interactive use usually sits at 6 concurrent streams (avg), spikes to ~35 during reporting windows, and once a week we run a 2-hr batch that simulates ~150 concurrent ephemeral requests (the batch jobs can be queued if needed).

Two asks: can you
1) Re-run the scenarios with 1.5M/day start and a weekly large batch job included?
2) Provide a short note on the trade-offs (latency vs $/token) when using continuous batching + prefix caching vs a more conservative per-request execution path?

Happy to jump back on a short call with Rishi and Monica next week.

—Elena

Thanks for the ping — I sketched two quick pricing scenarios and a short note on batching trade-offs. Summary below; I attached a one-page sketch to the Drive link.

Summary pricing sketches (very high level)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go):
  • Low: $420 / 1M tokens (no commit, continuous-batching enabled), assuming average batch size 12 tokens and 95p latency ~320ms.
  • Medium: $330 / 1M tokens (usage volume discounts kicking in at 5M/day sustained), 95p latency ~280ms with prefix caching.
  • High-volume (burstable): $260 / 1M tokens (negotiated tier, subject to commit + soft SLA), 95p latency ~250ms.

- Reserved Commit (6 months):
  • 3M/day equivalent commit: ~$240 / 1M tokens (predictable throughput, lower egress of small bursts).
  • 6M/day equivalent commit: ~$210 / 1M tokens (best-in-class unit econ for their target).

Batching + prefix-caching trade-offs (short note)
- Continuous batching with small windows (5–20ms max delay) and prefix/KV caching increases throughput and reduces per-token compute cost, which lowers $/1M. It works best for interactive flows with reasonably similar prefix patterns.
- Trade-off: to get lower $/1M you accept slightly higher p95 latency compared to pure single-request execution; pick knobs (max_batch_delay, max_batch_size) to hit your latency SLOs.
- For weekly large batch jobs we recommend routing those to a burst queue or separate dedicated pool to avoid widening interactive tail latency.

Next steps
1) Priya/Monica: update scenario workbook with 1.5M/day start + weekly batch job and upload.
2) I’ll prepare a vendor-facing pricing slide that maps expected spend bands to commit tiers and latency SLOs.
3) Priya: propose 30-min call with Elena + Marcus for Tue/Wed next week.
